metadata.title: The Kelley-Meka bounds for sets free of three-term arithmetic progressions

extraction_notes.note: The five sketch steps are stated in tcolorbox boxes (not theorem environments); each is a claim, attributed to Kelley-Meka (Step 4 to Croot-Sisask/Schoen-Sisask), linked by specializes edges to the precise lemmas of Sections 2-3.
Proof sketches in Section 1: the sketch rule asks for rigor semi_formal but rigor is not allowed on proofs; no rigor was set. PP5 is the only argument for Theorem 2 (no alternative flag).
Origin: the sifting lemma is marked external (proof 'identical to that in KM'); the unbalancing lemma is kept paper since its proof differs from Kelley-Meka's.

Cited results only mentioned qualitatively (Schoen-Sisask four-variable bounds, Sanders' subspace in S, KM Questions 6.2 and A.4) and the claim that Theorem 4 'can be proved in a very similar way' got no nodes.

nodes.name: Non-trivial three-term progression
nodes.statement: (Non-trivial here means that $d\neq 0$.)

nodes.name: Roth's theorem
nodes.statement: Let $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ be a set which does not contain any (non-trivial) three-term arithmetic progressions. Even establishing that $\lvert A\rvert = o(N)$ is a difficult problem, this being Roth's landmark 1953 result \cite{Ro}.
assumptions: $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ be a set which does not contain any (non-trivial) three-term arithmetic progressions
conclusions: $\lvert A\rvert = o(N)$

nodes.name: Bloom-Sisask bound beyond the logarithmic barrier
nodes.statement: Since Roth's work there has been a sequence of quantitative improvements to the upper bound, all of the form $\lvert A\rvert \leq N/(\log N)^{C}$ for some constant $C>0$, culminating in recent work of the authors \cite{BS}, who showed that $C=1+c$ is permissible, where $c>0$ is some tiny constant (we refer to the introduction of \cite{BS} for further history).
nodes.statement_short: Roth-type bound $\lvert A\rvert \leq N/(\log N)^{1+c}$ for 3AP-free $A$, via Bloom-Sisask.
conclusions: $C=1+c$ is permissible, where $c>0$ is some tiny constant

nodes.name: Kelley-Meka theorem
nodes.statement: If $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ contains no non-trivial three-term arithmetic progressions, then \[\abs{A} \leq \frac{N}{\exp\left(c(\log N)^{1/12}\right)}\] for some absolute constant $c>0$.
assumptions: $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ contains no non-trivial three-term arithmetic progressions
conclusions: \[\abs{A} \leq \frac{N}{\exp\left(c(\log N)^{1/12}\right)}\] for some absolute constant $c>0$
nodes.label: th-main-int

nodes.name: Behrend's construction
nodes.statement: Indeed, we know that there are subsets of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ of size at least $\exp(-c(\log N)^{1/2})N$, where $c>0$ is some universal constant, that contain no non-trivial three-term progressions.
conclusions: there are subsets of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ of size at least $\exp(-c(\log N)^{1/2})N$

nodes.name: Kelley-Meka theorem in finite fields
nodes.statement: If $q$ is an odd prime and $A\subseteq \mathbb{F}_q^n$ has no non-trivial three-term progressions, then $\lvert A\rvert \leq q^{n-cn^{1/9}}$ for some constant $c>0$.
conclusions: $\lvert A\rvert \leq q^{n-cn^{1/9}}$ for some constant $c>0$
nodes.label: th-main-ff

nodes.name: Ellenberg-Gijswijt bound
nodes.statement: The utility of Theorem~\ref{th-main-ff} is as a demonstration of the proof techniques, since for the result itself a stronger bound of $\lvert A\rvert \leq q^{n-cn}$ is available via the polynomial method, as shown by Ellenberg and Gijswijt \cite{EG}.
conclusions: a stronger bound of $\lvert A\rvert \leq q^{n-cn}$ is available via the polynomial method

nodes.name: Long arithmetic progressions in A+A+A
nodes.statement: If $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ has size $\alpha N$, then $A+A+A$ contains an arithmetic progression of length \[\geq \exp(-C\log(2/\alpha)^3)N^{c/\log(2/\alpha)^{9}},\] where $C,c>0$ are constants.
conclusions: $A+A+A$ contains an arithmetic progression of length \[\geq \exp(-C\log(2/\alpha)^3)N^{c/\log(2/\alpha)^{9}},\]
nodes.label: th-3A

nodes.name: Sanders' bound for progressions in A+A+A
nodes.statement: For comparison, the previously best bound known was $N^{\alpha^{1+o(1)}}$, originally due to Sanders \cite{Sa1}.

nodes.name: Freiman-Halberstam-Ruzsa construction
nodes.statement: A construction due to Freiman, Halberstam, and Ruzsa \cite{FHR} shows that no exponent better than $c/\log(2/\alpha)$ is possible.

nodes.name: Normalised indicator function
nodes.statement: It is convenient to introduce the notion of a normalised indicator function: if $A\subseteq G$ is non-empty with size $\lvert A\rvert=\alpha \lvert G\rvert$ then we write $\mu_A=\alpha^{-1}\ind{A}$.
also_stated_at: We write $\mu_A=\alpha^{-1}\ind{A}$ for the normalised indicator function of $A$ (so that $\norm{\mu_A}_1=1$).

nodes.name: Indicator function
nodes.statement: (For a set $A$, we write $1_A$ for the indicator function of $A$, taking the value $1$ on $A$ and $0$ elsewhere.)

nodes.name: Local L^p(V) norm
nodes.statement: If $V\subseteq G$ and $1\leq p<\infty$, then we denote the $L^p(V)$ norm of $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$ by \[\norm{f}_{p(\mu_V)} = \brac{\frac{1}{\abs{V}} \sum_{x \in V} \abs{f(x)}^p}^{1/p}.\]

nodes.name: Average of the convolution over a subgroup
nodes.statement: An elementary calculation shows that, when $V\leq G$ is a subgroup and $A\subseteq V$, \[\norm{\mu_A\ast \mu_A}_{1(\mu_V)}=\frac{\abs{G}}{\abs{V}}=\norm{\mu_V}_{1(\mu_V)}.\]
assumptions: $V\leq G$ is a subgroup and $A\subseteq V$
conclusions: \[\norm{\mu_A\ast \mu_A}_{1(\mu_V)}=\frac{\abs{G}}{\abs{V}}=\norm{\mu_V}_{1(\mu_V)}.\]

nodes.name: Kelley-Meka structure theorem in finite fields
nodes.statement: Let $\epsilon>0$. There is a constant $C=C(\epsilon)>0$ such that the following holds. Let $G=\mathbb{F}_q^n$ for some prime $q$ and $n\geq 1$. Let $p\geq 1$. For any non-empty $A\subseteq G$ with $\abs{A}=\alpha \abs{G}$ there exists a subspace $V\leq G$ with \[\mathrm{codim}(V)\leq Cp^4\log(2/\alpha)^5\] and $x \in G$ such that, if $A' =(A-x)\cap V$, then \begin{enumerate} \item $\abs{A'}\geq (1-\epsilon)\alpha \abs{V}$ and \item $\norm{\mu_{A'}\ast \mu_{A'}-\mu_V}_{p(\mu_V)} \leq \epsilon \frac{\abs{G}}{\abs{V}}$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Any dense A in F_q^n has a translate whose restriction to a low-codimension subspace V keeps its density and has L^p-flat self-convolution.
conclusions: there exists a subspace $V\leq G$ with \[\mathrm{codim}(V)\leq Cp^4\log(2/\alpha)^5\]
$\abs{A'}\geq (1-\epsilon)\alpha \abs{V}$
$\norm{\mu_{A'}\ast \mu_{A'}-\mu_V}_{p(\mu_V)} \leq \epsilon \frac{\abs{G}}{\abs{V}}$.
nodes.label: th-ff-gen

nodes.name: Kelley-Meka structure theorem relative to Bohr sets
nodes.statement: There is a constant $c>0$ such that the following holds. Let $\delta,\epsilon\in (0,1)$, let $p \geq 1$ and let $k$ be a positive integer such that $(k,\abs{G})=1$. There is a constant $C=C(\epsilon,\delta,k)>0$ such that the following holds. For any finite abelian group $G$ and any subset $A\subseteq G$ with $\abs{A}=\alpha \abs{G}$ there exists a regular Bohr set $B$ with \[\mathrm{rk}(B)\leq Cp^4\log(2/\alpha)^5\] and \[\abs{B}\geq \exp\left(-Cp^5\log(2p/\alpha)\log(2/\alpha)^6\right)\abs{G}\] and $A' \subseteq (A-x)\cap B$ for some $x\in G$ such that \begin{enumerate} \item $\abs{A'}\geq (1-\epsilon)\alpha \abs{B}$, \item $\abs{A'\cap B'}\geq (1-\epsilon)\alpha\abs{B'}$, where $B'=B_{\rho}$ is a regular Bohr set with $\rho\in (\tfrac{1}{2},1)\cdot c\delta\alpha/dk$, and \item \[\norm{(\mu_{A'}-\mu_B)\ast (\mu_{A'}- \mu_B)}_{p(\mu_{k\cdot B'})} \leq \epsilon\frac{\abs{G}}{\abs{B}}.\] \end{enumerate}
nodes.section: The general group case: Bohr sets
nodes.statement_short: For any dense A in a finite abelian group there is a low-rank regular Bohr set B on which a translate of A keeps its density (also on a narrower B') and has L^p-balanced convolution.
assumptions: Let $\delta,\epsilon\in (0,1)$, let $p \geq 1$ and let $k$ be a positive integer such that $(k,\abs{G})=1$.
any finite abelian group $G$ and any subset $A\subseteq G$ with $\abs{A}=\alpha \abs{G}$
conclusions: there exists a regular Bohr set $B$ with \[\mathrm{rk}(B)\leq Cp^4\log(2/\alpha)^5\]
$\abs{A'}\geq (1-\epsilon)\alpha \abs{B}$
$\abs{A'\cap B'}\geq (1-\epsilon)\alpha\abs{B'}$
\[\norm{(\mu_{A'}-\mu_B)\ast (\mu_{A'}- \mu_B)}_{p(\mu_{k\cdot B'})} \leq \epsilon\frac{\abs{G}}{\abs{B}}.\]
nodes.label: th-int-gen

nodes.name: Variants of the measure in Theorem 5
nodes.statement: An identical proof gives a statement with the measure $\mu_{k\cdot B'}$ in part (3) replaced by $\mu_{k\cdot B'+t}$ for any $t\in B$, or indeed $\mu_B$ or $\mu_B\ast \mu_B$, the latter two of which may appear more natural.

nodes.name: Improved exponents
nodes.statement: Indeed, a small modification of the method as presented in this paper allows for a slight improvement: the $1/12$ of Theorem~\ref{th-main-int} can be replaced by $1/9$ with a relatively clean argument (the only modification required is to the almost-periodicity part). A further tedious lengthy technical optimisation allows for an exponent of $5/41$. Since the focus of this paper is an exposition of the method and results of Kelley and Meka, we will detail these improvements in a separate forthcoming note. The same modification leads to an improvement of the exponent in Theorem~\ref{th-main-ff} from $1/9$ to $1/7$, and an improvement of the exponent in Theorem~\ref{th-3A} from $9$ to $7$.
nodes.statement_short: The method gives exponent 1/9 (and 5/41 with more work) in Theorem 1, 1/7 in Theorem 2 and 7 in Theorem 3; details deferred to a forthcoming note.

nodes.name: Natural limit of the method
nodes.statement: We believe that an exponent of $1/7$ (in the statement of Theorem~\ref{th-main-int}) is the natural limit of these methods, in that achieving anything better will require significant new ideas.

nodes.name: Logarithmic abbreviation L(alpha)
nodes.statement: Logarithmic factors will appear often, and so in this paper we use the convenient abbreviation $\lo{\alpha}$ to denote $\log(2/\alpha)$.

nodes.name: Normalised counting measure, inner product and L^p norm
nodes.statement: We use the normalised counting measure on $G$, so that \[\langle f,g\rangle = \mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits_{x\in G}f(x)\overline{g(x)}\textrm{ and }\norm{f}_p=\brac{\mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits_{x\in G}\abs{f(x)}^p}^{1/p}\textrm{ for }1\leq p<\infty,\] where $\mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits_{x\in G}=\frac{1}{\lvert G\rvert}\sum_{x\in G}$.
nodes.statement_short: Inner product and L^p norms on G use the normalised counting (expectation) measure.

nodes.name: Convolution and difference convolution
nodes.statement: For any $f,g:G\to \mathbb{C}$ we define the convolution and the difference convolution\footnote{We caution that, while convolution is commutative and associative, difference convolution is in general neither.} as \[f\ast g(x)=\mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits_y f(y)g(x-y)\quad\textrm{and}\quad f\circ g(x)=\mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits_yf(x+y)\overline{g(y)}.\]

nodes.name: Adjoint property
nodes.statement: Note the useful adjoint property \[\langle f, g\ast h\rangle = \langle f\circ h,g\rangle.\]
conclusions: \[\langle f, g\ast h\rangle = \langle f\circ h,g\rangle.\]

nodes.name: k-fold convolution
nodes.statement: We furthermore write $f^{(p)}$ for the $p$-fold convolution $f^{(p)} = f*f*\cdots*f$, where there are $p$ copies of $f$.

nodes.name: Weighted inner product and L^p norm
nodes.statement: For some purposes it is conceptually cleaner to work relative to other non-negative functions on $G$, so that if $\mu:G\to\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ has $\norm{\mu}_1=1$ we write \[\langle f,g\rangle_\mu = \mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits_{x\in G}\mu(x)f(x)\overline{g(x)}\textrm{ and }\norm{f}_{p(\mu)}=\brac{\mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits_{x\in G}\mu(x)\abs{f(x)}^p}^{1/p}\textrm{ for }1\leq p<\infty.\]

nodes.name: Density relative to a measure
nodes.statement: We use the slight abuse of notation that if $\mu:G\to \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ with $\norm{\mu}_1=1$, then $\mu(A)=\norm{\ind{A}}_{1(\mu)}$ is the density of $A$ relative to $\mu$.

nodes.name: Relative density
nodes.statement: We will sometimes speak of $A\subseteq B$ with relative density $\alpha=\abs{A}/\abs{B}$.

nodes.name: Fourier transform and dual group
nodes.statement: The Fourier transform of $f:G\to\mathbb{R}$ is $\widehat{f}:\widehat{G}\to \mathbb{C}$ defined for $\gamma\in\widehat{G}$ as \[\widehat{f}(\gamma)=\mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits_{x\in G}f(x)\overline{\gamma(x)},\] where $\widehat{G} = \{ \gamma : G \to \mathbb{C}^\times : \text{$\gamma$ a homomorphism} \}$ is the dual group of $G$.

nodes.name: Convolution on the dual group
nodes.statement: We will also use convolution of functions $f, g : \widehat{G} \to \mathbb{C}$, defined as $f\ast g(\gamma) = \sum_{\chi \in \widehat{G}} f(\chi)g({\gamma-\chi})$, and denote $k$-fold convolution again by $f^{(k)}$ for such functions.\footnote{Note that we are using additive notation for the group operation on $\widehat{G}$.}

nodes.name: Elementary Fourier facts
nodes.statement: We note the following elementary facts: \begin{itemize} \item $\widehat{f\ast g}=\widehat{f}\cdot \widehat{g}$ and $\widehat{f\circ f}=\Abs{\widehat{f}}^2$ (so in particular the Fourier transform of $f\circ f$ is a non-negative function on $\widehat{G}$), \item $\mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits_x f(x)^k = \widehat{f}\ast\cdots \ast\widehat{f}(0_{\widehat{G}})$, where the convolution is $k$-fold, and \item if $\mu:G\to\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ has $\norm{\mu}_1=1$, then the Fourier transform of $\mu-1$ is $\widehat{\mu}\ind{\neq 0_{\widehat{G}}}$. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Fourier transform turns convolution into products, k-th moments into k-fold dual convolutions at 0, and kills the mean of a probability density.

nodes.name: Spectral non-negativity consequences
nodes.statement: Note that these three facts immediately imply that the Fourier transform of $\mu_A\circ \mu_A-1$ is non-negative, that $\mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits (\mu_A\circ \mu_A-1)^k \geq 0$ for any integer $k$, and (coupled with the triangle inequality) that $\norm{\mu_A\ast \mu_A-1}_p\leq \norm{\mu_A\circ \mu_A-1}_p$ when $p$ is an even integer.
nodes.statement_short: mu_A o mu_A - 1 has non-negative Fourier transform and moments, and dominates the L^p norm of mu_A * mu_A - 1 for even p.
conclusions: the Fourier transform of $\mu_A\circ \mu_A-1$ is non-negative
$\norm{\mu_A\ast \mu_A-1}_p\leq \norm{\mu_A\circ \mu_A-1}_p$ when $p$ is an even integer

nodes.name: Vinogradov notation
nodes.statement: Finally, we use the Vinogradov notation $X \ll Y$ to mean $X = O(Y)$, that is, there exists some constant $C>0$ such that $\abs{X}\leq CY$.

nodes.name: Asymptotic notation asymp and Omega
nodes.statement: We write $X\asymp Y$ to mean $X\ll Y$ and $Y\ll X$, and $X=\Omega(Y)$ to mean $Y = O(X)$.

nodes.name: Sets A and C of the sketch
nodes.statement: Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{F}_q^n$ be a set of density $\alpha$ and $C\subseteq \mathbb{F}_q^n$ a set of density $\gamma$.

nodes.name: Step 1: Hölder lifting
nodes.statement: If $\langle \mu_A\ast \mu_A, \mu_{C}\rangle \leq 1/2$, then $\norm{\mu_A\circ \mu_A-1}_p\geq 1/4$ for some $p\ll \lo{\gamma}$.
conclusions: $\norm{\mu_A\circ \mu_A-1}_p\geq 1/4$ for some $p\ll \lo{\gamma}$

nodes.name: Proof of Step 1
nodes.statement:
This is essentially a one-line application of H"{o}lder's inequality: \[	frac{1}{2}\leq \abs{\langle \mu_A\ast \mu_A-1,\mu_Cangle} \leq 
orm{\mu_A\ast \mu_A-1}_p
orm{\mu_C}_{p/(p-1)}\leq 2
orm{\mu_A\ast \mu_A-1}_p\] for sufficiently large $p$, since $
orm{\mu_C}_{p/(p-1)}=\gamma^{-1/p}$, and noting that $
orm{\mu_A\ast \mu_A-1}_p\leq 
orm{\mu_A\circ \mu_A-1}_p$ when $p$ is an even integer.
nodes.statement_short: One application of Hölder's inequality, using the L^p comparison of * and o for even p.

nodes.name: Step 2: Unbalancing
nodes.statement:
For any $f:G	o \mathbb{R}$ such that $\widehat{f}\geq 0$, if $
orm{f}_p\geq 1/4$, then $
orm{f+1}_{p'}\geq 1+1/8$ for some $p'\ll p$. In particular, if $
orm{\mu_A\circ \mu_A-1}_p\geq 1/4$, then $
orm{\mu_A\circ \mu_A}_{p'}\geq 1+1/8$.
conclusions: $\norm{f+1}_{p'}\geq 1+1/8$ for some $p'\ll p$

nodes.name: Shkredov's physical proof of unbalancing
nodes.statement: We remark that, as pointed out to the authors by Shkredov, an entirely physical proof of this step is possible, with no mention of the Fourier transform at all, if we replace the assumption $\widehat{f}\geq 0$ with $f=g\circ g$ for some function $g:\mathbb{R}\to \mathbb{C}$ (note that this is indeed satisfied in our application since $\mu_A\circ \mu_A-1=(\mu_A-1)\circ (\mu_A-1)$). We refer to the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem-key-spec} for details.

nodes.name: Fourier route to the unbalanced L^p bound
nodes.statement: At this point we digress to note that, instead of following Steps 1 and 2 as Kelley and Meka do, one could obtain the conclusion $\norm{\mu_A\circ \mu_A}_p\geq 1+\Omega(1)$ for some $p\ll \lo{\gamma}$ from the assumption that $\langle \mu_A\ast \mu_A,\mu_C\rangle \leq 1/2$ using more classical Fourier-based methods.
nodes.statement_short: Classical Fourier methods give $\norm{\mu_A\circ\mu_A}_p\geq 1+\Omega(1)$ for some $p\ll\lo{\gamma}$ directly from few solutions.

nodes.name: Fourier proof of the digression
nodes.statement: By converting the inner product to Fourier space and applying the triangle inequality we observe that \[1/2\leq \sum_{\lambda\neq 0}\abs{\widehat{\mu_A}(\lambda)}^2\abs{\widehat{\mu_C}(\lambda)}.\] It follows that, for some choice of signs $c_\lambda\in\mathbb{C}$, we have \[1+1/2\leq \sum_\lambda \abs{\widehat{\mu_A}(\lambda)}^2\abs{\widehat{\mu_{C}}(\lambda)}=\mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits_{x\in C}\sum_{\lambda}c_\lambda \abs{\widehat{\mu_A}(\lambda)}^2\lambda(-x).\] Applying H\"{o}lder's inequality to the left-hand side and using orthogonality of characters yields, for any even integer $p$, \[1+1/2\leq \gamma^{-1/p}\brac{\sum_{\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_{p}}c_{\lambda_1}\cdots \overline{c_{\lambda_{p}}}\abs{\widehat{\mu_A}(\lambda_1)}^2\cdots \abs{\widehat{\mu_A}(\lambda_{p})}^21_{\lambda_1+\cdots-\lambda_{p}=0}}^{1/p}.\] We can discard the signs $c_\lambda$ by the triangle inequality, and then by orthogonality the sum here is in fact equal to $\norm{\mu_A\circ \mu_A}_p$, and we are done choosing $p$ suitably large.
nodes.statement_short: Pass to Fourier space, insert signs, apply Hölder and orthogonality of characters to get an L^p norm of mu_A o mu_A.

nodes.name: Step 3: Dependent random choice
nodes.statement: If $\norm{\mu_A\circ \mu_A}_p\geq 1+1/8$, then there are $A_1,A_2\subseteq A$ of density at least $\alpha^{O(p)}$ such that \[\langle \mu_{A_1}\circ \mu_{A_2}, \ind{S}\rangle \geq 1-1/32\] where $S=\{ x : \mu_A\circ \mu_A(x) > 1+1/16\}$.
conclusions: there are $A_1,A_2\subseteq A$ of density at least $\alpha^{O(p)}$

nodes.name: Sketch of proof of Step 3 (sifting)
nodes.statement: The proof of this step, called sifting in \cite{KM}, is completely elementary, and uses dependent random choice -- one takes $A_i$ to be the intersection of $p$ randomly chosen translates of $A$. A simple expectation calculation combined with the $L^p$ information then verifies that there must exist some choice of translates which satisfy both the density conditions and the inner product condition.
nodes.statement_short: Dependent random choice: take A_i as intersections of p random translates of A and use an expectation calculation.

nodes.name: Step 4: Almost periodicity
nodes.statement: For any sets $A_1,A_2,S\subseteq\mathbb{F}_q^n$, if $A_1,A_2$ have density at least $\alpha$, then there is a subspace $V$ with codimension $O(\lo{\alpha}^4)$ such that \[\abs{\langle \mu_V\ast \mu_{A_1}\circ \mu_{A_2},\ind{S}\rangle - \langle \mu_{A_1}\circ \mu_{A_2},\ind{S}\rangle }\leq 1/100.\]
conclusions: there is a subspace $V$ with codimension $O(\lo{\alpha}^4)$

nodes.name: Step 5: Density increment
nodes.statement: If $\langle \mu_A\ast \mu_A,\mu_{C}\rangle \leq 1/2$, then there is an affine subspace $V$ of codimension $O(\lo{\alpha}^4\lo{\gamma}^4)$ on which $A$ has density at least $(1+\tfrac{1}{100})\alpha$.
conclusions: there is an affine subspace $V$ of codimension $O(\lo{\alpha}^4\lo{\gamma}^4)$ on which $A$ has density at least $(1+\tfrac{1}{100})\alpha$

nodes.name: Proof of Step 5
nodes.statement: This is just a trivial combination of the previous 4 steps (noting that the density increment condition can also be phrased as $\norm{\mu_A\ast \mu_V}_\infty \geq 1+1/100$).
nodes.statement_short: Combine Steps 1-4.

nodes.name: Deduction of Theorem 2 from the density increment
nodes.statement: For example, the deduction of Theorem~\ref{th-main-ff} is routine with $C=2\cdot A$. Indeed, a density increment such as $\alpha\mapsto (1+\Omega(1))\alpha$ can occur at most $O(\lo{\alpha})$ many times, after which we must halt with many three-term arithmetic progressions found in the intersection of $A$ with some affine subspace, the codimension of which is bounded above by $O(\lo{\alpha}^9)$.
nodes.statement_short: Density increment iteration with C = 2.A: at most O(L(alpha)) increments before many 3APs appear.

nodes.name: Derivation of the A+A theorem
nodes.statement: Alternatively, carrying through these steps with $C$ being the complement of $A+A$ leads to the following.
nodes.statement_short: Run Steps 1-5 with C the complement of A+A.

nodes.name: Kelley-Meka theorem on A+A in finite fields
nodes.statement: If $A\subseteq \mathbb{F}_q^n$ has density $\alpha$ and $\gamma\in(0,1]$, then there is some affine subspace $V\leq \mathbb{F}_q^n$ of codimension $O(\lo{\alpha}^5\lo{\gamma}^4)$ such that \[\abs{(A+A)\cap V}\geq (1-\gamma)\abs{V}.\]
conclusions: there is some affine subspace $V\leq \mathbb{F}_q^n$ of codimension $O(\lo{\alpha}^5\lo{\gamma}^4)$ such that \[\abs{(A+A)\cap V}\geq (1-\gamma)\abs{V}.\]

nodes.name: Sanders' bound for A+A in finite fields
nodes.statement: For comparison, the best bound previously available, due to Sanders \cite{Sa2}, had codimension $O(\lo{\alpha}^4\gamma^{-2})$.

Let $\epsilon\in(0,1)$ and $

nodes.statement: Let $C_{\epsilon}, D_{\epsilon,\delta} \geq 1$ be parameters to be specified later, and let $c$ be the smaller of $1/2$ and the constant $c$ in Proposition~\ref{prop-it}. Let $t\geq 0$ be maximal such that there is a sequence of regular Bohr sets, say $B^{(0)},\ldots,B^{(t)}$, and subsets of translates of $A$, say $A_0,\ldots,A_t$, such that the following holds: \begin{enumerate} \item $B^{(0)}=G$ and $A_0=A$, \item each $B^{(i)}$ is a regular Bohr set of rank $d_i$ and \[d_{i+1}\leq d_i + C_{\epsilon} \lo{\alpha}^4p^4\] and \[\Abs{B^{(i+1)}}\geq \exp(-D_{\epsilon,\delta}(dp\lo{\alpha/d}+\lo{\alpha}^5p^5))\Abs{B^{(i)}},\] and \item each $A_i$ is a subset of $B^{(i)}$ with density $\alpha_i$ such that $\alpha_{i+1}\geq (1+c\epsilon/4)\alpha_i$ for $0\leq i<t$. \end{enumerate} Observe from point (3), and the trivial fact that $\alpha_i\leq 1$, that $t\ll_\epsilon \lo{\alpha}$. Note that this implies $d_t\ll_{\epsilon} \lo{\alpha}^5p^4$. We apply Lemma~\ref{lem-bour} with $c\epsilon/2$ in place of $\epsilon$, and $B=B^{(t)}$, $B'=B_{c'\alpha\epsilon/d_t}$ and $B''=B'_{c''\delta\alpha/d_t}$, where the constants are in particular chosen to ensure that $B',B''$ are both regular. Provided we pick $D_{\epsilon,\delta}$ large enough in terms of $C_{\epsilon}$, $\epsilon$, and $\delta$, Lemma~\ref{lemma:bohrsiz} and the maximality of $t$ ensure that we must be in the first alternative of Lemma~\ref{lem-bour}'s conclusion: there exists a translate $A_t-x$ such that $\abs{(A_t-x)\cap B'}\geq (1-c\epsilon/2)\alpha \abs{B'}$ and $\abs{(A_t-x)\cap B''}\geq (1-c\epsilon/2)\alpha\abs{B''}$. We claim that $A'=(A_t-x)\cap B'$, with the $B'$ and $B''$ above playing the role of $B$ and $B'$ respectively, satisfies the conclusions of Theorem~\ref{th-flat-on-bohr}. Indeed, the bounds on the rank and size of $B'$, and the density conditions on $A'$, are clearly satisfied. This a contradiction to the maximality of $t$, provided $C_{\epsilon}$ matches the implicit constant in the first $O_{\epsilon}$-term, since we can take $B^{(t+1)}=\tilde{B}$ and $A_{t+1}=(A_t-y)\cap \tilde{B}$, noting that by Lemma~\ref{lemma:bohrsiz} \[\abs{B''''}\geq \exp(-O_{\epsilon,\delta}(d\lo{\alpha/d_t)})\Abs{B^{(t)}}.\]

nodes.name: Deduction of the Kelley-Meka theorem from the counting version
nodes.statement: Theorem~\ref{th-main-int} is an immediate consequence of the following result that gives a lower bound for the number of three-term arithmetic progressions in an arbitrary set, coupled with the observation that if $A$ contains only trivial three-term arithmetic progressions then this count is at most $N$.
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from the 3AP counting theorem, since a set with only trivial 3APs has at most N of them.

nodes.name: Kelley-Meka counting theorem
nodes.statement: If $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ has size $\abs{A}=\alpha N$, then $A$ contains at least \[\exp(-O(\lo{\alpha}^{12}))N^2\] many three-term arithmetic progressions.
conclusions: $A$ contains at least \[\exp(-O(\lo{\alpha}^{12}))N^2\] many three-term arithmetic progressions.

nodes.name: Proof of the counting theorem
nodes.statement: As usual, we begin by considering $A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ as a subset of $G=\mathbb{Z}/(2N+1)\mathbb{Z}$ -- the density of this set within $G$ is still $\asymp \alpha$, and any three-term arithmetic progression in $A\subseteq G$ yields one in $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$. We apply Theorem~\ref{th-int-gen} with $\epsilon=1/4$, $k=2$, and $p=\lceil K\lo{\alpha}\rceil$ for some large constant $K$. Let $A''=A'\cap B'$. If \[\langle \mu_{A'}\ast \mu_{A'},\mu_{2\cdot A''}\rangle \geq \tfrac{1}{2}\mu(B)^{-1}\] we are done, since the left-hand side is at most $\ll\alpha^{-3}\mu(B)^{-2}\mu(B')^{-1}$ times the number of three-term arithmetic progressions in $A$, and by Lemma~\ref{lemma:bohrsiz} we have \[\mu(B)\mu(B')\geq \exp(-O_\epsilon(\lo{\alpha}^{12})).\] Otherwise, we are in the second case of Proposition~\ref{prop-holder}, which contradicts the conclusion of Theorem~\ref{th-int-gen}, and we are done.
nodes.statement_short: Embed in Z/(2N+1)Z, apply the Bohr-set structure theorem with k=2, and use Bohr-set Hölder lifting to count 3APs.

nodes.statement: As in the previous section, Theorem \ref{th-3A} follows immediately from the following statement for general groups, by embedding $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ in a cyclic group $\mathbb{Z}/M\mathbb{Z}$ for a prime $M$ between $2N$ and $4N$.

nodes.statement: We apply Theorem~\ref{th-int-gen} with $\epsilon=1/4$, $k=1$, and $p=\lceil K\lo{\alpha}\rceil$ for some large constant $K$. Let $B,B'$ be the Bohr sets produced by that conclusion, and $A' = (A-x) \cap B$ the corresponding restricted translate of $A$. We first argue that $\abs{(A'+A')\cap B'}\geq (1-\alpha/4)\abs{B'}$. Indeed, otherwise if we let $C=B'\backslash (A'+A')$, then the first case of Proposition~\ref{prop-holder} is violated and the conclusion of Theorem~\ref{th-int-gen} means the second also cannot hold. Let $B''=B'_{c\alpha/d}$, where $c>0$ is some small constant. We argue that $B''\subseteq A'+A'+A'$. If not, there is some $x\in B''$ such that $(A'+A')\cap (x-A')=\emptyset$, and so \[\abs{A'\cap(B'-x)}=\abs{(x-A')\cap B'}\leq \abs{B'\backslash (A'+A')}\leq \tfrac{\alpha}{4}\abs{B'}.\] By regularity, however, the left-hand side is at least \[\abs{A'\cap B'}-\abs{B\backslash (B'-x)}\geq \abs{A'\cap B'}-\tfrac{1}{4}\alpha \abs{B'}\geq \tfrac{\alpha}{2}\abs{B'},\] which is a contradiction. We have found some Bohr set $B''$ of rank $O(\lo{\alpha}^{9})$ and density \[\mu(B'')\geq \exp(-O(\lo{\alpha}^{12}))\] such that $B''\subseteq A'+A'+A'$. nodes.statement: We now present the alternative physical proof of \eqref{eq-nonneg}, assuming $f=g\circ g$ and $\nu=h\circ h$. This argument was pointed out to the authors by Shkredov, who has made extensive use of the following kind of manipulations (for example in \cite{Sh}). We observe that \begin{align*} \langle \nu, f^k\rangle &= \mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits_x h\circ h(x)g\circ g(x)^k\\ &= \mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits_{y_1,y_2}h(y_1)\overline{h(y_2)}\brac{\mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits_z g(y_1+z)\overline{g(y_2+z)}}^k\\ &=\mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits_{z_1,\ldots,z_k}\mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits_{y_1,y_2}h(y_1)\overline{h(y_2)}g(y_1+z_1)\cdots \overline{g(y_2+z_k)}\\ &= \mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits_{z_1,\ldots,z_k}\abs{\mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits_y h(y)g(y+z_1)\cdots g(y+z_k)}^2, \end{align*} which is clearly non-negative as each summand is.
nodes.statement_short: Physical proof by expanding into squares

nodes.name: Reduce to odd p >= 5
nodes.statement: We now show how \eqref{eq-nonneg} implies the conclusion. Without loss of generality we can assume that $p\geq 5$ is an odd integer.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to odd p >= 5

Using \eqref{eq-nonneg}, since $2\max(x,0)=x+\abs{x}$ for $x\in\mathbb{R}$ and $f^{p-1}=\abs{f}^{p-1}$, we have \[2\langle \max(f,0),f^{p-1}angle_
u=\langle 
u,f^pangle+\langle \abs{f},f^{p-1}angle_
u\geq

u)}^p\geq \epsilon^p.\] Therefore, if $P=\{ x : f(x) \geq 0\}$, then $\langle \ind{P},f^{p}angle_
u\geq  rac{1}{2}\epsilon^{p}$.

nodes.name: Restrict to the large-value set T and apply Cauchy-Schwarz
nodes.statement:
Furthermore, if $T=\{ x\in P : f(x) \geq 	frac{3}{4}\epsilon\}$, then $\langle \ind{P ackslash T},f^pangle_

On the other hand, by the triangle inequality \[
orm{f}_{2p(
u)}\leq 1+

It follows that, for any $p'\geq 1$, \[
orm{f+1}_{p'(
u)}\geq \langle \ind{T},\abs{f+1}^{p'}angle_
u^{1/p'}\geq (1+	frac{3}{4}\epsilon)(\epsilon/10)^{2p/p'}.\] The desired bound now follows if we choose $p'$ a sufficiently large multiple (depending on $\epsilon$) of $p$.

nodes.name: Define A_i(s) and expand the moment over random shifts
nodes.statement: For $s\in G^{p}$ let $A_1(s)=B_1\cap (A+s_1)\cap\cdots\cap (A+s_{p})$, and similarly for $A_2(s)$. Note that \begin{align*} \langle (\mu_A\circ \mu_A)^p, f\rangle_\mu &=\mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits_{\substack{b_1\in B_1\\ b_2\in B_2}}\mu_A\circ \mu_A(b_1-b_2)^{p}f(b_1-b_2)\\ &=\mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits_{\substack{b_1\in B_1\\ b_2\in B_2}}\brac{\alpha^{-2}\mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits_{t\in G}\ind{A+t}(b_1)\ind{A+t}(b_2)}^{p}f(b_1-b_2)\\ &=\alpha^{-2p}\mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits_{\substack{b_1\in B_1\\ b_2\in B_2}}\mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits_{s\in G^p}\ind{A_1(s)}(b_1)\ind{A_2(s)}(b_2)f(b_1-b_2)\\ &=\tfrac{\alpha^{-2p}\abs{G}^2}{\abs{B_1}\abs{B_2}}\mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits_{s\in G^p}\langle \ind{A_1(s)}\circ \ind{A_2(s)}, f\rangle. \end{align*}
nodes.section: 2.2 An application of dependent random choice
nodes.statement_short: Define A_i(s) and expand the moment over random shifts

nodes.name: Specialise to f = 1 and define eta
nodes.statement: In particular, applying this with $f\equiv 1$ we see that, if $\alpha_i(s)=\abs{A_i(s)}/\abs{G}$, then \[\norm{\mu_A\circ \mu_A}_{p(\mu)}^p=\tfrac{\alpha^{-2p}\abs{G}^2}{\abs{B_1}\abs{B_2}}\mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits_s \alpha_1(s)\alpha_2(s)\] and \[\frac{\langle (\mu_A\circ \mu_A)^p,f\rangle_\mu}{\norm{\mu_A\circ \mu_A}_{p(\mu)}^p}=\frac{\mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits_{s}\langle \ind{A_1(s)}\circ \ind{A_2(s)}, f\rangle}{\mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits_s \alpha_1(s)\alpha_2(s)}=\eta,\] say.
nodes.section: 2.2 An application of dependent random choice
nodes.statement_short: Specialise to f = 1 and define eta

nodes.name: Discard shifts with small density product
nodes.statement: Note that, if \[M=\tfrac{1}{2}\alpha^p(\abs{B_1}\abs{B_2}/\abs{G}^2)^{1/2}\norm{\mu_A\circ \mu_A}_{p(\mu)}^p,\] then \begin{align*} \mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits_s 1_{\alpha_1(s)\alpha_2(s)<M^2}\alpha_1(s)\alpha_2(s) &< M\brac{\mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits_s \mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits_{x\in G}1_{A_1(s)}(x)}^{1/2}\brac{\mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits_s \mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits_{x\in G}1_{A_2(s)}(x)}^{1/2}\\ &= M\alpha^p(\abs{B_1}\abs{B_2}/\abs{G}^2)^{1/2}=\frac{1}{2}\mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits_s \alpha_1(s)\alpha_2(s) \end{align*} and so \[\mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits_s\langle \ind{A_1(s)}\circ \ind{A_2(s)},f\rangle =\eta \mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits \alpha_1(s)\alpha_2(s)\\ < 2\eta \mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits_s \alpha_1(s)\alpha_2(s)1_{\alpha_1(s)\alpha_2(s)\geq M^2}.\]
nodes.section: 2.2 An application of dependent random choice
nodes.statement_short: Discard shifts with small density product

nodes.name: Pick a good shift s
nodes.statement: In particular there must exist some $s$ such that \[\langle \ind{A_1(s)}\circ \ind{A_2(s)},f\rangle< 2\eta \alpha_1(s)\alpha_2(s)1_{\alpha_1(s)\alpha_2(s)\geq M^2},\] and the claim follows (note that the left-hand side is trivially $\geq 0$ and hence such an $s$ must satisfy $\alpha_1(s)\alpha_2(s)\geq M^2$).
nodes.section: 2.2 An application of dependent random choice
nodes.statement_short: Pick a good shift s

nodes.name: Apply Lemma drc with f the indicator of G minus S
nodes.statement: The deduction of Lemma~\ref{lem-sift} is immediate from Lemma~\ref{lem-drc} with $f=\ind{G\backslash S}$.
nodes.section: 2.2 An application of dependent random choice
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma drc with f the indicator of G minus S

nodes.name: Assume p large and even
nodes.statement: Indeed, by nesting of $L^p$ norms we can assume that $p$ is sufficiently large in terms of $\epsilon$ and $\delta$ (this is where the $O_{\epsilon,\delta}(1)$ term arises in the exponent), and that $p$ is an even integer.
nodes.section: 2.2 An application of dependent random choice
nodes.statement_short: Assume p large and even

nodes.name: Bound the mass outside S
nodes.statement: It then suffices to note that \[\langle \mu_{A_1}\circ \mu_{A_2},\ind{S}\rangle=1-\langle \mu_{A_1}\circ \mu_{A_2},\ind{G\backslash S}\rangle\] and by definition of $S$ we have \[\frac{\langle (\mu_A\circ \mu_A)^{p},\ind{G\backslash S}\rangle}{\norm{\mu_A\circ \mu_A}_{p}^p}\leq (1-\epsilon)^p\] which is $\leq \delta/2$ if $p$ is large enough.
nodes.section: 2.2 An application of dependent random choice
nodes.statement_short: Bound the mass outside S

nodes.name: Apply Hölder's inequality
nodes.statement: If the first alternative fails, then by H\"{o}lder's inequality, for any $p\geq 1$ \[\epsilon < \abs{ \langle \mu_A \ast \mu_A - 1, \mu_C \rangle } \leq \norm{\mu_A\ast \mu_A-1}_p\gamma^{-1/p}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Apply Hölder's inequality

nodes.name: Choose p ~ L(gamma)
nodes.statement: In particular, if we choose $p=2\lceil K\lo{\gamma}\rceil$ for some large constant $K$, then we deduce that \[\norm{\mu_A\ast \mu_A-1}_{p}\geq \tfrac{1}{2}\epsilon.\]
nodes.statement_short: Choose p ~ L(gamma)

nodes.name: Compare * and o norms via Fourier
nodes.statement_short: Compare * and o norms via Fourier

nodes.name: Set up a physical argument
nodes.statement: Again, although we have used a one-line Fourier proof here, this can also be seen using an entirely physical argument, which we sketch here. Note that $\mu_A\ast \mu_A-1=(\mu_A-1)\ast (\mu_A-1)$ and similarly for $\mu_A\circ \mu_A-1$.
nodes.statement_short: Set up a physical argument

nodes.name: Reduce to ||f*f||_p <= ||f o f||_p
nodes.statement: It suffices therefore to show that, for any function $f:G\to\mathbb{C}$, we have \[\norm{f\ast f}_p^p\leq \norm{f\circ f}_p^p.\]
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to ||f*f||_p <= ||f o f||_p

nodes.name: Expand both sides and apply Cauchy-Schwarz
nodes.statement: We can write the left-hand side as \begin{align*} \norm{f\ast f}_p^p &= \mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits_{x,y}\brac{\mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits_{u}f(x+u)f(y-u)}^p\\ &=\mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits_{u_1,\ldots,u_p}\brac{\mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits_x f(x+u_1)\cdots f(x+u_p)}\brac{\mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits_y f(y-u_1)\cdots f(y-u_p)} \end{align*} and the right-hand side as \begin{align*} \norm{f\circ f}_p^p &= \mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits_{x,y}\brac{\mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits_{u}f(x+u)\overline{f(y+u)}}^p\\ &=\mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits_{u_1,\ldots,u_p}\abs{\mathop{ \mathchoice{\vcenter{\hbox{\larger[4]$\mathbb{E}$}}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} {\kern0pt\mathbb{E}} }\displaylimits_x f(x+u_1)\cdots f(x+u_p)}^2, \end{align*} and the desired inequality now follows from the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality.
nodes.statement_short: Expand both sides and apply Cauchy-Schwarz

nodes.name: Apply Hölder lifting
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem-ff1}, if the first alternative fails, then $\norm{\mu_A\circ \mu_A-1}_p\geq \epsilon/2$ for some $p\ll \lo{\gamma}$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Hölder lifting

nodes.name: Apply unbalancing
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem-key-spec} (applied to $f=\mu_A\circ \mu_A-1$) we deduce that $\norm{\mu_A\circ \mu_A}_p\geq 1+\epsilon/4$ for some $p\ll_\epsilon \lo{\gamma}$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply unbalancing

nodes.name: Apply sifting
nodes.statement: Hence, by Corollary~\ref{cor-key}, there are $A_1,A_2$, both of density \[\geq \alpha^{O_\epsilon(\lo{\gamma})},\] such that $\langle \mu_{A_1}\circ \mu_{A_2},\ind{S}\rangle \geq 1-\epsilon/32$, where $S=\{x : \mu_A\circ \mu_A(x)\geq 1+\epsilon/8\}$ .
nodes.statement_short: Apply sifting

nodes.name: Apply almost-periodicity
nodes.statement: By Theorem~\ref{th-ap} there is a subspace $V$ of the required codimension such that \[\langle \mu_V\ast \mu_{A_1}\circ \mu_{A_2},\ind{S}\rangle \geq 1-\tfrac{1}{16}\epsilon.\]
nodes.statement_short: Apply almost-periodicity

nodes.name: Average to get the density increment
nodes.statement:
By definition of $S$, it follows that  egin{align*} 1+\Omega(\epsilon) &\leq (1+\epsilon/8)(1-\epsilon/16)\ &\leq \langle \mu_V\ast \mu_{A_1}\circ \mu_{A_2},\mu_A\circ \mu_Aangle\ &\leq 
orm{\mu_V\ast \mu_A}_\infty 
orm{\mu_{A}\ast \mu_{A_2}\circ \mu_{A_1}}_1\ &= 
orm{\mu_V\ast \ind{A}}_\infty \alpha^{-1}, \end{align*} and the proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Average to get the density increment

nodes.name: Introduce a maximal density-increment chain
nodes.statement: Let $C_{\epsilon}, D_{\epsilon,\delta} \geq 1$ be parameters to be specified later, and let $c$ be the smaller of $1/2$ and the constant $c$ in Proposition~\ref{prop-it}. Let $t\geq 0$ be maximal such that there is a sequence of regular Bohr sets, say $B^{(0)},\ldots,B^{(t)}$, and subsets of translates of $A$, say $A_0,\ldots,A_t$, such that the following holds:
nodes.statement_short: Introduce a maximal density-increment chain

nodes.name: Rank and size condition on the chain
nodes.statement: each $B^{(i)}$ is a regular Bohr set of rank $d_i$ and \[d_{i+1}\leq d_i + C_{\epsilon} \lo{\alpha}^4p^4\] and \[\Abs{B^{(i+1)}}\geq \exp(-D_{\epsilon,\delta}(dp\lo{\alpha/d}+\lo{\alpha}^5p^5))\Abs{B^{(i)}},\] and
nodes.statement_short: Rank and size condition on the chain

nodes.name: Density increment condition on the chain
nodes.statement: each $A_i$ is a subset of $B^{(i)}$ with density $\alpha_i$ such that $\alpha_{i+1}\geq (1+c\epsilon/4)\alpha_i$ for $0\leq i<t$.
nodes.statement_short: Density increment condition on the chain

nodes.name: Bound the chain length and final rank
nodes.statement: Observe from point (3), and the trivial fact that $\alpha_i\leq 1$, that $t\ll_\epsilon \lo{\alpha}$. Note that this implies $d_t\ll_{\epsilon} \lo{\alpha}^5p^4$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound the chain length and final rank

nodes.name: Apply Bourgain narrowing
nodes.statement: We apply Lemma~\ref{lem-bour} with $c\epsilon/2$ in place of $\epsilon$, and $B=B^{(t)}$, $B'=B_{c'\alpha\epsilon/d_t}$ and $B''=B'_{c''\delta\alpha/d_t}$, where the constants are in particular chosen to ensure that $B',B''$ are both regular. Provided we pick $D_{\epsilon,\delta}$ large enough in terms of $C_{\epsilon}$, $\epsilon$, and $\delta$, Lemma~\ref{lemma:bohrsiz} and the maximality of $t$ ensure that we must be in the first alternative of Lemma~\ref{lem-bour}'s conclusion: there exists a translate $A_t-x$ such that $\abs{(A_t-x)\cap B'}\geq (1-c\epsilon/2)\alpha \abs{B'}$ and $\abs{(A_t-x)\cap B''}\geq (1-c\epsilon/2)\alpha\abs{B''}$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Bourgain narrowing

nodes.name: Claim A' satisfies the conclusions
nodes.statement: We claim that $A'=(A_t-x)\cap B'$, with the $B'$ and $B''$ above playing the role of $B$ and $B'$ respectively, satisfies the conclusions of Theorem~\ref{th-flat-on-bohr}. Indeed, the bounds on the rank and size of $B'$, and the density conditions on $A'$, are clearly satisfied.
nodes.statement_short: Claim A' satisfies the conclusions

nodes.name: Assume the L^p flatness fails
nodes.statement: Suppose for a contradiction that \[\norm{\mu_{A'}\circ \mu_{A'}}_{p(\mu_{k\cdot B'''}\circ \mu_{k\cdot B'''}\ast \mu_{k\cdot B''''}\circ \mu_{k\cdot B''''})}\geq (1+\epsilon)\mu(B')^{-1},\] for some regular Bohr sets $B''' = B''_\rho$ and $B''''=B'''_{\rho'}$ satisfying $\rho,\rho'\in(\frac{1}{2},1)\cdot c\delta \alpha/d_t$.
nodes.statement_short: Assume the L^p flatness fails

nodes.name: Apply the iterative proposition
nodes.statement: The conditions of Proposition~\ref{prop-it} are met, and hence we deduce there is some $\tilde{B}\subseteq B''''$ of rank \[\mathrm{rk}(\tilde{B})\leq \mathrm{rk}(B)+O_{\epsilon}(\lo{\alpha}^4p^4)\] and \[\Abs{\tilde{B}}\geq \exp(-O_{\epsilon}(d_tp\lo{\alpha/d_t}+\lo{\alpha}^5p^5))\Abs{B''}\] and there is a translate of $A_t$, say $A_t-y$, such that \[\mu_{\tilde{B}}(A_t-y)\geq (1+c\epsilon)(1-c\epsilon/2)\alpha\geq (1+c\epsilon/4)\alpha,\] say.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the iterative proposition

nodes.name: Contradict maximality of t
nodes.statement: This a contradiction to the maximality of $t$, provided $C_{\epsilon}$ matches the implicit constant in the first $O_{\epsilon}$-term, since we can take $B^{(t+1)}=\tilde{B}$ and $A_{t+1}=(A_t-y)\cap \tilde{B}$, noting that by Lemma~\ref{lemma:bohrsiz} \[\abs{B''''}\geq \exp(-O_{\epsilon,\delta}(d\lo{\alpha/d_t)})\Abs{B^{(t)}}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Contradict maximality of t

nodes.name: Apply Schoen-Sisask Theorem 5.4
nodes.statement: We apply \cite[Theorem 5.4]{SS} with the choices (with apologies for the unfortunate clash in variable naming between papers) \[A\to -A_2,\quad M\to A_1,\quad L\to -S,\quad S\to B'_{c/d},\quad B\to B'_{c/d}\] and note that \[\Abs{-A_2+B'_{c/d}}\leq \Abs{B'+B'_{c/d}}\leq 2\abs{B'}\leq 2\alpha_2^{-1}\abs{A_2}\] by regularity of $B'$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Schoen-Sisask Theorem 5.4

nodes.name: Match the parameters
nodes.statement: The statement now almost follows from \cite[Theorem 5.4]{SS} after observing that (in that theorem's language) we have $K\leq 2\alpha_2^{-1}$, $\sigma=1$, and $\eta\geq \alpha_1/2$, except that there the statement has a constraint on the rank and the width of $B''$, rather than the rank and the size.
nodes.statement_short: Match the parameters

nodes.name: Convert width to size
nodes.statement: Nonetheless the width condition can be immediately converted into a lower bound for the size of $B''$ with Lemma~\ref{lemma:bohrsiz}.
nodes.statement_short: Convert width to size

nodes.name: Localise by averaging
nodes.statement: By averaging there exists some $x\in k\cdot B'+k\cdot B''$ such that \[\norm{\mu_A\circ \mu_{A}}_{p(\mu_{k\cdot B'}\ast \mu_{k\cdot B''-x})}\geq (1+\epsilon)\mu(B)^{-1}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Localise by averaging

nodes.name: Apply sifting
nodes.statement: We now apply Lemma~\ref{lem-sift} with $B_1=k\cdot B'$ and $B_2=k\cdot B''+x$. This produces some $A_1\subseteq k\cdot B'$ and $A_2\subseteq k\cdot B''-x$ such that, with $S=\{x : \mu_{A}\circ \mu_A(x)\geq (1+\epsilon/2)\mu(B)^{-1}\}$, \[\langle \mu_{A_1}\circ \mu_{A_2},\ind{S}\rangle \geq 1-\epsilon/4\] and \[\min\brac{\frac{\abs{A_1}}{\abs{B'}},\frac{\abs{A_2}}{\abs{B''}}}\gg \alpha^{2p+O_{\epsilon}(1)}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Apply sifting

nodes.name: Apply Bohr-set almost-periodicity
nodes.statement: We now apply Theorem~\ref{th-ap-int} (with $k\cdot B'$ and $k\cdot B''$ playing the roles of $B$ and $B'$ respectively), noting that we can, without loss of generality, take $S$ to be supported in $A_1-A_2\subseteq k\cdot B'+k\cdot B''-x$ and so by regularity of $B'$ \[\abs{S}\leq \abs{B'+B''}\leq 2\abs{B'}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Apply Bohr-set almost-periodicity

nodes.name: Lower bound the smoothed inner product
nodes.statement: This produces some $B'''\subseteq k\cdot B''$ of the required rank and size such that \[\langle \mu_{B'''}\ast \mu_{A_1}\circ \mu_{A_2},\mu_A\circ \mu_A\rangle\geq (1+\epsilon/2)(1-\epsilon/4)(1-\epsilon/8)\mu(B)^{-1}\geq (1+c\epsilon)\mu(B)^{-1}\] for some absolute constant $c>0$.
nodes.statement_short: Lower bound the smoothed inner product

nodes.name: Average to get the increment
nodes.statement:
The result now follows from averaging, since \[\langle \mu_{B'''}\ast \mu_{A_1}\circ \mu_{A_2},\mu_A\circ \mu_Aangle\leq 
orm{\mu_{B'''}\ast \mu_{A}}_\infty
orm{\mu_{A_2}\circ \mu_{A_1}\ast \mu_A}_1=
orm{\mu_{B'''}\ast \mu_{A}}_\infty.\]
nodes.statement_short: Average to get the increment

nodes.name: Introduce g and split by the triangle inequality
nodes.statement:
Let us write \[ g =\mu_A\circ \mu_B + \mu_B \circ \mu_A - \mu_B\circ\mu_B \] and note that for any $p'\geq 1$  egin{align*} 
orm{ \mu_{A}\circ \mu_{A}}_{p'(
u)} &= 
orm{ (\mu_A-\mu_B)\circ (\mu_A-\mu_B) + \mu(B)^{-1} + g - \mu(B)^{-1} }_{p'(
u)} \ &\geq 
orm{ (\mu_A-\mu_B)\circ (\mu_A-\mu_B) + \mu(B)^{-1} }_{p'(
u)} - 
orm{ g - \mu(B)^{-1} }_{p'(
u)}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Introduce g and split by the triangle inequality

nodes.name: Bound the error term by regularity
nodes.statement:
To bound the error term, note that $\mu_A\circ \mu_B(0) = \mu(B)^{-1}$ and that by regularity (for example with Lemma~ef{lemma:regConv}), for $x \in \mathrm{supp}(
u)$,  egin{align*} \abs{\mu_A\circ\mu_B(x) - \mu_A\circ\mu_B(0)} &\leq \alpha^{-1} \mu(B)^{-1} 
orm{\mu_B(\cdot+x) - \mu_B}_1 \ &\llho \mathrm{rk}(B) \alpha^{-1} \mu(B)^{-1} \ &\leq 	frac{1}{12} \epsilon \mu(B)^{-1}, \end{align*} say, assuming $ho$ is sufficiently small, and similarly for the other terms constituting $g$. Hence \[
orm{g-\mu(B)^{-1}}_{p'(
u)}\leq 
orm{g - \mu(B)^{-1}}_{L^\infty(\mathrm{supp}(
u))} \leq 	frac{1}{4}\epsilon\,\mu(B)^{-1}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Bound the error term by regularity

nodes.name: Reduce to the balanced part
nodes.statement: It therefore suffices to find some $p'\ll_\epsilon p$ such that \[\norm{ (\mu_A-\mu_B)\circ (\mu_A-\mu_B) + \mu(B)^{-1} }_{p'(\nu)}\geq (1+\tfrac{1}{2}\epsilon)\mu(B)^{-1}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to the balanced part

nodes.name: Apply the unbalancing lemma
nodes.statement: This is immediate from Lemma~\ref{lem-key-spec} applied to $f=\mu(B)(\mu_A-\mu_B)\circ (\mu_A-\mu_B)$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the unbalancing lemma

nodes.name: Dominate mu_B by a smoothed measure
nodes.statement: By an application of Lemma \ref{lemma:fourierbohr} with $L=4$, $\rho = c/4\mathrm{rk}(B)$ and $\nu=\mu_{B'}\ast \mu_{B'}\ast \mu_{B''}\ast\mu_{B''}$, we have \begin{align*} \mu_B &\leq 2\mu_{B_{1+4\rho}}*\nu. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Dominate mu_B by a smoothed measure

nodes.name: Rewrite the norm as an average over translates
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the norm as an average over translates

nodes.name: Pick t and compare via Fourier positivity
nodes.statement_short: Pick t and compare via Fourier positivity

nodes.name: WLOG delta small
nodes.statement: We may, without loss of generality, assume that $\delta$ is sufficiently small in terms of $\epsilon$ and $k$.
nodes.statement_short: WLOG delta small

nodes.name: Choose p' and apply flatness on a Bohr set
nodes.statement: Let $p'\ll_\epsilon p$ satisfy the condition in Proposition~\ref{prop:Lp_orth}. Let $A'$ and $B$ be the regular Bohr sets provided by Theorem~\ref{th-flat-on-bohr} applied with $p$ replaced by $p'$ and $\epsilon$ replaced by $\epsilon/8$.
nodes.statement_short: Choose p' and apply flatness on a Bohr set

nodes.name: Verify the conclusion by contradiction
nodes.statement:
We claim that this choice satisfies the conclusion of Theorem~ef{th-int-gen}. It suffices to prove \[
orm{(\mu_{A'}-\mu_B)\ast(\mu_{A'}-\mu_B)}_{p(\mu_{k\cdot B'})}\leq \epsilon \mu(B)^{-1}.\] Suppose not. Let $B''=B'_{ho}$ and $B'''=B''_{ho'}$ be regular Bohr sets with $ho=c_1/d$ and $ho'=c_2/d$ for some sufficiently small constants $c_1,c_2>0$. By Proposition~ef{prop:pos_def_measures} we have, if we let $f=\mu_{A'}-\mu_B$ for brevity, \[
orm{f\ast f}_{p(\mu_{k\cdot B'})}\leq 2 
orm{f\circ f}_{p(
u)}\] where $
u=\mu_{k\cdot B''}\circ \mu_{k\cdot B''}\ast \mu_{k\cdot B'''}\circ \mu_{k\cdot B'''}$. In particular, $
orm{f \circ f}_{p(
u)}>	frac{1}{2}\epsilon\mu(B)^{-1}$, and so by Proposition~ef{prop:Lp_orth} (noting that $
u$ is supported on $k(B''+B''+B'''+B''')\subseteq B'_{4kho}\subseteq B_{c/d}$) we deduce that \[
orm{\mu_{A'}\circ \mu_{A'}}_{p'(
u)} \geq (1+\epsilon/8)\mu(B)^{-1},\] which contradicts the conclusion of Theorem~ef{th-flat-on-bohr}, and we are done.
nodes.statement_short: Verify the conclusion by contradiction

nodes.name: State the claim and reduce to an L^p bound
nodes.statement: We claim that this choice satisfies the conclusion of Theorem~\ref{th-int-gen}. It suffices to prove \[\norm{(\mu_{A'}-\mu_B)\ast(\mu_{A'}-\mu_B)}_{p(\mu_{k\cdot B'})}\leq \epsilon \mu(B)^{-1}.\]
nodes.statement_short: State the claim and reduce to an L^p bound

nodes.name: Assume the bound fails and introduce narrower Bohr sets
nodes.statement: Suppose not. Let $B''=B'_{\rho}$ and $B'''=B''_{\rho'}$ be regular Bohr sets with $\rho=c_1/d$ and $\rho'=c_2/d$ for some sufficiently small constants $c_1,c_2>0$.
nodes.statement_short: Assume the bound fails and introduce narrower Bohr sets

nodes.name: Pass to a positive definite measure
nodes.statement:
By Proposition~ef{prop:pos_def_measures} we have, if we let $f=\mu_{A'}-\mu_B$ for brevity, \[
orm{f\ast f}_{p(\mu_{k\cdot B'})}\leq 2 
orm{f\circ f}_{p(
u)}\] where $
u=\mu_{k\cdot B''}\circ \mu_{k\cdot B''}\ast \mu_{k\cdot B'''}\circ \mu_{k\cdot B'''}$.
nodes.statement_short: Pass to a positive definite measure

nodes.name: Apply Bohr-set unbalancing and contradict flatness
nodes.statement:
In particular, $
orm{f \circ f}_{p(
u)}>	frac{1}{2}\epsilon\mu(B)^{-1}$, and so by Proposition~ef{prop:Lp_orth} (noting that $
u$ is supported on $k(B''+B''+B'''+B''')\subseteq B'_{4kho}\subseteq B_{c/d}$) we deduce that \[
orm{\mu_{A'}\circ \mu_{A'}}_{p'(
u)} \geq (1+\epsilon/8)\mu(B)^{-1},\] which contradicts the conclusion of Theorem~ef{th-flat-on-bohr}, and we are done.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Bohr-set unbalancing and contradict flatness

nodes.name: Expand around mu_B
nodes.statement: We first note that \[\langle \mu_A\ast \mu_A,\mu_C\rangle = \langle (\mu_A-\mu_B)\ast(\mu_A-\mu_B),\mu_C\rangle+2\langle \mu_A\ast \mu_B,\mu_C\rangle -\langle \mu_B\ast \mu_B,\mu_C\rangle.\]
nodes.statement_short: Expand around mu_B

nodes.name: Control cross terms by regularity
nodes.statement:
By the regularity of $B$ (more specifically Lemma~ef{lemma:regConv}) and the fact that $C\subseteq B_{c\epsilon /\mathrm{rk}(B)}$, we have \[\abs{\langle \mu_B\ast \mu_B,\mu_Cangle-\mu(B)^{-1}}\leq 
orm{\mu_B}_\infty
orm{\mu_B\ast \mu_C-\mu_B}_1\leq 	frac{1}{8}\epsilon \mu(B)^{-1}.\] Similarly, the fact that $C\subseteq B_{c\epsilon \alpha/\mathrm{rk}(B)}$ implies that \[\abs{\langle \mu_A\ast \mu_B,\mu_Cangle-\mu(B)^{-1}}\leq 
orm{\mu_A}_\infty
orm{\mu_B\ast \mu_C-\mu_B}_1\leq 	frac{1}{16}\epsilon \mu(B)^{-1}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Control cross terms by regularity

nodes.name: Combine the error bounds
nodes.statement: It follows that, with $f=(\mu_A-\mu_B)\ast (\mu_A-\mu_B)$, we have \[\abs{\langle \mu_A\ast \mu_A,\mu_C\rangle-\mu(B)^{-1}-\langle f,\mu_C\rangle}\leq \tfrac{1}{4}\epsilon\mu(B)^{-1}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Combine the error bounds

nodes.name: Apply Hölder's inequality
nodes.statement: Therefore, if the first possibility fails, then \[\gamma^{-1}\abs{\langle f, \ind{C}\rangle_{\mu_{B'}}}=\abs{\langle f,\mu_C\rangle}\geq\tfrac{3}{4}\epsilon\mu(B)^{-1}.\] By H\"{o}lder's inequality, for any $p\geq 1$, \[\norm{f}_{p(\mu_{B'})}\gamma^{1-1/p}\geq \abs{\langle f,\ind{C}\rangle_{\mu_{B'}}}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Apply Hölder's inequality

nodes.name: Choose p ~ L(gamma)
nodes.statement: We can choose some $p\ll \lo{\gamma}$ such that $\gamma^{-1/p}\leq 3/2$, and the proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Choose p ~ L(gamma)

nodes.name: Embed in Z/(2N+1)Z
nodes.statement: As usual, we begin by considering $A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ as a subset of $G=\mathbb{Z}/(2N+1)\mathbb{Z}$ -- the density of this set within $G$ is still $\asymp \alpha$, and any three-term arithmetic progression in $A\subseteq G$ yields one in $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$.
nodes.statement_short: Embed in Z/(2N+1)Z

nodes.name: Apply the Bohr-set structure theorem
nodes.statement: We apply Theorem~\ref{th-int-gen} with $\epsilon=1/4$, $k=2$, and $p=\lceil K\lo{\alpha}\rceil$ for some large constant $K$. Let $A''=A'\cap B'$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the Bohr-set structure theorem

nodes.name: Case: many solutions, count 3APs
nodes.statement: If \[\langle \mu_{A'}\ast \mu_{A'},\mu_{2\cdot A''}\rangle \geq \tfrac{1}{2}\mu(B)^{-1}\] we are done, since the left-hand side is at most $\ll\alpha^{-3}\mu(B)^{-2}\mu(B')^{-1}$ times the number of three-term arithmetic progressions in $A$, and by Lemma~\ref{lemma:bohrsiz} we have \[\mu(B)\mu(B')\geq \exp(-O_\epsilon(\lo{\alpha}^{12})).\]
nodes.statement_short: Case: many solutions, count 3APs

nodes.name: Case: few solutions contradicts the structure theorem
nodes.statement: Otherwise, we are in the second case of Proposition~\ref{prop-holder}, which contradicts the conclusion of Theorem~\ref{th-int-gen}, and we are done.
nodes.statement_short: Case: few solutions contradicts the structure theorem

nodes.name: Apply the structure theorem with k=1
nodes.statement: We apply Theorem~\ref{th-int-gen} with $\epsilon=1/4$, $k=1$, and $p=\lceil K\lo{\alpha}\rceil$ for some large constant $K$. Let $B,B'$ be the Bohr sets produced by that conclusion, and $A' = (A-x) \cap B$ the corresponding restricted translate of $A$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the structure theorem with k=1

nodes.name: A'+A' covers most of B'
nodes.statement: We first argue that $\abs{(A'+A')\cap B'}\geq (1-\alpha/4)\abs{B'}$. Indeed, otherwise if we let $C=B'\backslash (A'+A')$, then the first case of Proposition~\ref{prop-holder} is violated and the conclusion of Theorem~\ref{th-int-gen} means the second also cannot hold.
nodes.statement_short: A'+A' covers most of B'

nodes.name: Introduce the narrower Bohr set B''
nodes.statement: Let $B''=B'_{c\alpha/d}$, where $c>0$ is some small constant. We argue that $B''\subseteq A'+A'+A'$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce the narrower Bohr set B''

nodes.name: Contradiction via regularity
nodes.statement: If not, there is some $x\in B''$ such that $(A'+A')\cap (x-A')=\emptyset$, and so \[\abs{A'\cap(B'-x)}=\abs{(x-A')\cap B'}\leq \abs{B'\backslash (A'+A')}\leq \tfrac{\alpha}{4}\abs{B'}.\] By regularity, however, the left-hand side is at least \[\abs{A'\cap B'}-\abs{B\backslash (B'-x)}\geq \abs{A'\cap B'}-\tfrac{1}{4}\alpha \abs{B'}\geq \tfrac{\alpha}{2}\abs{B'},\] which is a contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: Contradiction via regularity

nodes.name: Find a long AP via Lemma bohrap
nodes.statement: We have found some Bohr set $B''$ of rank $O(\lo{\alpha}^{9})$ and density \[\mu(B'')\geq \exp(-O(\lo{\alpha}^{12}))\] such that $B''\subseteq A'+A'+A'$. It remains to note that $A'+A'+A'$ is contained in a translate of $A+A+A$ and to appeal to Lemma~\ref{lem-bohrap} to find an arithmetic progression in $B''$ of length \[\geq \exp(-O(\lo{\alpha}^3))N^{\Omega(1/\lo{\alpha}^{9})}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Find a long AP via Lemma bohrap

nodes.name: Choose rho and apply the size bound
nodes.statement: Let $\rho=4(2/\abs{B})^{1/d}$, and note that by Lemma~\ref{lemma:bohrsiz} we have \[\abs{B_\rho}\geq (\rho/4)^d\abs{B}=2.\]
nodes.statement_short: Choose rho and apply the size bound

nodes.name: Multiples of x give an AP
nodes.statement: In particular there exists some $x\in B_\rho\backslash \{0\}$. By the triangle inequality it is clear that $\{x,\ldots,\lfloor \rho^{-1}\rfloor x\}\subseteq B$, whence $B$ contains an arithmetic progression of length $\gg \rho^{-1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Multiples of x give an AP
